ALT read dilution: tissue dilution in sampled pools

Why some families’ BC2S3 samples read too little donor ALT: the dilution factor per sample, mexicana chr10 (run 1273053; 2026-10-16)

Author

Fausto Rodríguez-Zapata

Published

October 16, 2026

The question

Each BC2S3 sample is a tissue pool: one leaf punch from each of six plants of one NIL, assumed to give equimolar DNA (docs/TERMINOLOGY.md). The sample introgression dosage check (docs/decisions.md, 2026-10-11) splits the 42 mexicana families of run 1273053 into two sets: families with balanced tissue pools (their samples read the expected ALT in donor segments) and with unbalanced tissue pools (too little ALT). The deficit is one-sided: no family reads too much ALT. Random unequal plant contributions would push dosage both ways, so something lowers the donor reads systematically. Candidates: dilution (other tissue or B73 DNA in the pool), selection against carriers during line development, mapping bias.

The dilution factor

For each sample and donor-segment state, the dilution factor is the observed ALT read frequency divided by the expected one; the expected one is the read-weighted ALT frequency of the families with balanced tissue pools (HET segments 41.1 %, ALT segments 86.3 %). States with fewer than 100 reads are left out.

  • ALT segments (donor allele in all six plants): the factor is about 1 in a balanced pool and falls with any admixed tissue. It is the clean dilution measure.
  • HET segments (the six plants segregate): the factor varies by segregation inside the pool even without dilution.
  • Dilution lowers both by the same factor (the diagonal). Selection and mapping bias act on loci, not on the whole sample, so they do not keep the two equal.
families samples HET factor, median ALT factor, median REF background, median ALT %
unbalanced 95 0.63 0.83 1.2
balanced 58 1.00 1.00 1.2

What it shows

  • Balanced families: ALT factor near 1 (median 1), HET factor spread by segregation; the two are unrelated (r = 0.09).
  • Unbalanced families: both factors lower (medians 0.63 and 0.83) and moving together (r = 0.47). 4 samples sit on the diagonal with an ALT factor below 0.65: diluted pools.
  • REF background is the same in both (1.2 %). Tissue from another donor family would raise it; B73 or recurrent-parent tissue would not. So the dilution, where present, is B73-like.

Limits

  • Only 43 of 153 samples have both factors: many samples carry no ALT segment on chr10.
  • Selection is not tested here; it needs the deficit per region across families (recurring low windows, stronger in ALT than in HET segments).
  • One chromosome, one taxon.
